objective:
Review and revise this Sol-authored implementation plan for a built-in iOS Simulator in BB.

Product frame: A user working in a thread opens the secondary panel's New Tab page and chooses an Action row labeled “Open simulator” with a Smartphone icon. This replaces the transient New Tab with one persistent, closable Simulator tab tied to the thread's environment. If no session exists, the tab shows a device picker and primary “Start simulator” button. Starting boots the chosen real Apple CoreSimulator through the enrolled environment Mac and then shows a live interactive phone surface. Reopening focuses the existing simulator tab. A later discoverability enhancement may add a thread-header phone icon, but the draft MVP avoids another permanent header control.

Technical architecture: Add a core `simulator` fixed-panel tab kind and `SimulatorTabContent`. Add typed environment simulator APIs and SDK area methods for availability, device list, attach/status, tap, gesture, type, hardware button, rotate, accessibility tree, screenshot, and stop. Add `bb simulator ...` commands which default to the current BB environment and accept `--environment` and `--device`. The server resolves the environment's host and dispatches typed online RPC commands. The host daemon owns a `SimulatorManager`, macOS/Xcode capability checks, environment-to-UDID session registry, packaged serve-sim executable resolution, helper health/reuse, and cleanup. Increment HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION.

Streaming/security: Do not expose serve-sim's full preview server because it contains host-exec routes and permissive CORS. The daemon should expose only allowlisted stream/config/input endpoints behind an unguessable short-lived lease. Same-host standalone can use a same-origin server proxy or loopback lease; enrolled remote Macs use BB's existing shared-port tunnel. Tokens must not be logged or persisted. Hidden tabs stop consuming frames but do not automatically shut down the device. Closing the tab releases its viewer lease; an explicit Stop action shuts down BB's managed helper/device. The MVP may initially support the primary/server-local Mac if secure remote transport materially expands scope, but contracts must preserve the environment host boundary.

Proposed tab states: (1) checking support; (2) unsupported host, with “iOS Simulator requires a Mac with Xcode” and no dead controls; (3) Xcode present but no runtimes/devices, with an Xcode recovery instruction; (4) ready/not running, device select + Start simulator; (5) starting, with stage text such as Booting/Connecting and cancel only if technically reliable; (6) live, with device name/state, Home, Rotate, Stop, interactive screen, and reconnect indicator; (7) recoverable error, preserving selection and showing Retry; (8) disconnected host, showing reconnect guidance without discarding the tab.

Scope proposal: MVP includes discovery, device selection, start/reuse, live MJPEG surface, pointer tap/drag/wheel gestures, keyboard/paste, Home, Rotate, Stop, screenshot, AX tree for agents, CLI/SDK parity, lifecycle cleanup, tests, and documentation/skill updates. Defer camera injection, permissions UI, multiple simultaneous devices per environment, Android, log streaming, WebKit inspector, and header shortcut. Prefer MJPEG first with frame dropping/backpressure and stream parking; leave AVCC/H.264 optimization for follow-up.

Please challenge the scope and user mental model, then return a revised comprehensive plan. Do not edit files or implement UI. This is the single resumable Fable Plan Council session; Sol retains final acceptance and implementation.
acceptance_checks: Identify any product or UX flaw that would make the simulator hard to discover, start, recover, or understand.
Decide whether the primary human entry point should be the New Tab Actions list, a persistent thread-header icon, or both, and explain the staged recommendation.
Evaluate the proposed environment-scoped ownership and tab/session lifecycle from a user's mental model.
Separate the smallest genuinely useful MVP from follow-up capabilities without omitting agent CLI/SDK parity.
Return an implementation-ready revised plan with explicit UI states, labels, controls, error recovery, accessibility expectations, and acceptance criteria.
route_reason: Model Relay selected a bounded Plan Council; Fable is reviewing product intent and UX while Sol owns technical discovery and implementation.
